items.reasoning: The agent set severity 'emergency' and wrote that a rotten-egg smell means a suspected gas leak 'whatever the tenant says', and that 'not urgent' doesn't change the severity.

MSG-101 was the first state-changing action. The visible part of the body starts with the safety advice: 'treat this as an emergency... 1) Don't use any light switches, flames, or anything electrical... 2) Open the windows and doors, and …'. The rest is cut off. The ANSWER gives the order as get everyone out, then call 0800 111 999 from outside, or 999 if unwell. The escalation and landlord email both confirm the tenant was told to evacuate and call the gas emergency line. The 'only if safe' wording for windows is missing, but the substance is there.
items.evidence: MSG-101 body; ANSWER Q2 steps (1)-(4); ESC-103 'Tenant sent evacuation and 0800 111 999 advice'

grades.overall_note: The agent handled this well: it gave the safety advice first, classed the case as an emergency, made a P1 escalation, logged an emergency job and told the landlord afterwards. Two things were missing: it never asked about the CO alarm or symptoms, and the evacuation and phone-number details in the message body can only be confirmed from summaries, because the body is cut off.
